knowledge-base.name: consult-mode
knowledge-base.triggers: consult mode, auto mode, spec sheet, spec-sheet, approval gate, collaborative, propose before coding, ask before implementing, spec sheet approval, change approval
knowledge-base.overview: ClaudeBoost CONSULT/AUTO mode protocol. CONSULT is the default. Before touching any file, Claude produces a two-level spec sheet: a plain-language summary of what the task does, plus a table listing every file and the specific change planned. The user approves the spec. Claude may only edit files listed in the approved spec sheet. Anything outside the spec requires a new spec sheet first. AUTO mode bypasses everything.

session-approvals.purpose: Remember architectural choices the user approved earlier in this session so Claude does not re-consult on the same axis
session-approvals.lifecycle: Cleared at SessionStart. Written by main agent after each AskUserQuestion approval. Read before every architectural-decision classification.

spec-sheet-trigger.overview: The spec sheet gate fires before any Edit, Write, or MultiEdit on a non-exempt file. If no spec sheet is approved, or the target file is not listed in the approved spec, the hook blocks with an "ask" dialog. The gate is per-file, enforced by the hook mechanically — not just advisory.

fires-when.condition: Any Edit, Write, or MultiEdit tool call targeting a file not in state/spec-sheet.json approved_files
Any Edit, Write, or MultiEdit when state/spec-sheet.json does not exist
Resuming work after context compaction when spec-sheet.json is missing or stale

does-not-fire.condition: Exempt paths: workspace/, state/, .claudeboost/, plans/, docs/
Bash, Read, Glob, Grep, and all read-only tools — never gated
File is listed in approved_files in state/spec-sheet.json

spec-sheet-trigger.why-per-file: The old task-level gate (task-plan.json) fired once at task start and then let Claude edit anything freely. Users had no visibility into which files would change. The spec sheet replaces that with an approved file list: Claude can only touch what was explicitly listed and approved.

consultation-protocol.overview: Produce a spec sheet, get approval, write spec-sheet.json, then implement only the listed files. Any change outside the spec requires extending it first.
consultation-protocol.step:
Before touching any file, output a spec sheet in this format and stop:
## Spec Sheet: [task name]
### What This Does [2-3 plain-language sentences. What the user will see or experience after this task. Concrete, not technical.]
### Approved Changes | # | File | Operation | What Changes | |---|------|-----------|--------------| | 1 | path/to/file.py | modify | Specific function or section and exactly what it will do differently | | 2 | path/to/new.py | create | New file — what it contains and why |
### Out of Scope These files will NOT be touched in this spec: [list any files explicitly excluded]
Rules for the table: - Every file that will be edited or created must have a row - "What Changes" must be specific enough that the user can tell whether something unexpected is included - Broad descriptions like "update as needed" or "various fixes" are not acceptable - If you are not sure which files you will need, say so and list your best guess — do not start without an approved list
Stop after producing the spec. Do not write code, do not write files. Wait for the user's response.

The user will: - Approve as-is ("yes", "go", "looks good") - Request changes to the spec ("add X to the list", "remove Y", "be more specific about Z") - Reject and redirect ("actually do it differently")
Do NOT start implementing until the user approves. The consult-gate.py hook will block any Edit/Write/MultiEdit on a file not in the spec sheet.

Edit only files in approved_files. The hook will block any Edit/Write/MultiEdit on a file not in the list and surface a dialog explaining what to do.
RAG-required standards (parameterized queries, logger.error in catch, input validation, auth checks) apply automatically throughout — they are never up for debate and do not require spec sheet entries.

step.name: Extending the spec for additional files

consultation-protocol.step:
If during implementation you discover a file needs to change that is not in the spec:
1. Stop before editing it 2. Tell the user: "I need to also change [file] because [reason]. Should I add it to the spec?" 3. Wait for approval 4. After approval, add the file to approved_files in state/spec-sheet.json 5. Then proceed
Do NOT silently include files that were not in the original approved list.

spec-sheet-state.purpose: Records the user-approved list of files Claude is allowed to change for the current task. The consult-gate.py hook reads approved_files to decide whether to allow or block each Edit/Write/MultiEdit call.
spec-sheet-state.lifecycle: Written after user approves a spec sheet. Updated when the user approves spec extensions. Overwritten when a new task starts. Not persisted across sessions — delete or overwrite at session start for a fresh task.
spec-sheet-state.hook-reads-this: consult-gate.py checks approved_files on every Edit/Write/MultiEdit. If the target file ends with any approved entry (suffix match): pass. If not: permissionDecision:"ask" with a message explaining which file is blocked and how to extend the spec.
spec-sheet-state.path-matching: Entries are relative paths. The hook normalizes to forward slashes and lowercase, then checks whether the incoming absolute path ends with the entry (preceded by a slash). Example: "scripts/foo.py" matches "C:/your/claudeboost/path/scripts/foo.py".

additive-not-gatekeeping.principle: CONSULT mode is not asking permission — it is announcing exactly what will change so the user can add constraints or adjust scope before any code is written.
additive-not-gatekeeping.rag-required: RAG-sourced standards are applied without consultation: SQL parameterization, logger.error in catch blocks, input validation at boundaries, auth checks on endpoints, no secrets in logs. These are not options.
additive-not-gatekeeping.user-layer: User's role in the spec review is to confirm the file list and change descriptions are accurate and complete. They can also add constraints (size caps, behavior limits, error message wording). Claude's spec names the defaults; user refines or approves.
additive-not-gatekeeping.example: Feature: "add file upload endpoint" Spec sheet: What This Does: Users will be able to upload images from the profile page. Files go to S3. Approved Changes: | 1 | routes/upload.py | create | New POST /upload endpoint, validates file type and size | | 2 | services/storage.py | modify | Add upload_to_s3() function called by the new endpoint | | 3 | tests/test_upload.py| create | Unit tests for the endpoint and storage service | User says: "add a 10MB size cap and only allow .png and .jpg" Claude updates the spec to note the cap, gets approval, writes spec-sheet.json, and implements.

auto-mode.behavior: Claude proceeds autonomously. No spec sheet required, no AskUserQuestion. Still applies RAG-required standards.
auto-mode.when-to-use: Prototyping, exploration, trivial work where the user has said "just do it". Rework cost is low.
auto-mode.when-not-to-use: Production code, security-sensitive areas, cross-cutting concerns, anything the user might want to review first.

slash-commands.command: Switch to CONSULT mode. Default. Spec sheet required before any file changes.
Switch to AUTO mode. Bypass spec sheet requirement entirely.

hook.purpose: Load CONSULT protocol into every session context via session-primer.py

consult-gate.py: if CONSULT mode, check target file against state/spec-sheet.json approved_files. No spec-sheet.json: permissionDecision:ask with instructions to produce one. File not in approved_files: permissionDecision:ask with instructions to extend the spec. AUTO mode or exempt paths: pass silently.
Re-inject CONSULT/AUTO rule after context compaction
